pr_comments: Upon seeing Github Actions CI, we seem to have a couple of issues with other test cases that invoke methods that eventually invoke the creation of a new timestamp in which one of their timestamps is nonexistent. For one of these, a `nonexistent = 'shift_forward'` parameter in `tz_localize` isn't accounted for in `__new__` and in another, nonexistent isn't directly accounted for in any parameters. A possible way to resolve this would be adding a `nonexistent` parameter to `Timestamp` or potentially to `__new__` that defaults at "raise", but I haven't had a lot of time to think through the feasibility of that. Let me know how you think we should address this.

> A possible way to resolve this would be adding a nonexistent parameter to Timestamp or potentially to __new__ that defaults at "raise", but I haven't had a lot of time to think through the feasibility of that. Let me know how you think we should address this.

We're pretty reticent to add new args to `Timestamp.__new__`, i think always raising is fine

issue_context.title: BUG: able to create nonexistent Timestamp
issue_context.body:
- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas.

- [X] (optional) I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas.

---

#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example

```python
import pandas as pd
ts = pd.Timestamp(year=2001, month=10, day=14, hour=0, minute=30, tz='America/Santiago')
print(ts)
```

#### Problem description

There was a [DST transition](https://www.timeanddate.com/time/change/chile/santiago?year=2001) on the 14th of October 2001, and the time from midnight to 1 a.m. does not exist. Ran into this while working on #40517 where we ran into an error while normalizing a `Timestamp` when midnight does not exist in a particular timezone. Yet, we are able to create this timestamp directly, even though it does not make any sense.

#### Expected Output

I would expect `NonExistentTimeError: 2001-10-14 00:30:00`

#### Notes

I wasn't able to find a prior issue for this. I'm a bit swamped right now, so I would appreciate if someone else looked at this bug. If no one takes it up, I'll investigate next week.

comments:
Might be the same core issue as discovered in https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/issues/40915#issuecomment-818460553

Generally. I think the `tz` argument in `Timestamp` (and `DatetimeIndex`, `date_range`) should be deprecated in favor of explicitly calling `tz_localize` and `tz_convert`
Take - Working with my team to contribute to this issue.
@rauniyars Thanks for taking this up! If you get stuck, don't hesitate to ask.

@AlexKirko do you know what method(s) for creating the time stamp our team should modify to add this error? We have found the [timestamp](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/7d4757b4deb851bb44ab6bb20cdc404fa13fffcf/pandas/_libs/tslibs/timestamps.pyx#L716) class and its cpython derivatives but we're still not sure where exactly to intervene.

@AlexKirko we have been looking through the timestamps and timezones classes for how the timezone validation of a new `Timestamp` is done, and haven't been able to pinpoint the specific issue so far. It seems like this issue isn't within `tz_localize` because the documentation of `tz_localize` has said that it is only used either when a `Timestamp` is being converted into another timezone or a timezone is being added to a naive `Timestamp`, and because the method hasn't been entered in our attempted print-statement-based tracing. We tried putting print statements at the top of the `TimeStamp`, `Timestamp._new_`, `tz_localize`, `maybe_get_tz`, `get_dst_info`, and `_get_utc_trans_times_from_dateutil_tz` methods, as well as on the `tz` and its type in `Timestamp.__new__`, and in each of the `if statements` for how `maybe_get_tz` handles strings, and received the following output:

```
>>> import pandas as pd
In class _Timestamp
In __new__
None
<class 'NoneType'>
In maybe_get_tz
In __new__
None
<class 'NoneType'>
In maybe_get_tz
>>> ts = pd.Timestamp(year=2001, month=10, day=14, hour=0, minute=30, tz='America/Santiago')
In __new__
America/Santiago
<class 'str'>
In maybe_get_tz
5
In maybe_get_tz
```

This output seemed to confirm that localized wasn't likely involved in the creation of a new timestamp. We did some further experimentation with a [nonexistent time](https://www.timeanddate.com/time/change/usa) in the United States and had it seemingly accept that timestamp's creation but that same timestamp when a time zone was assigned to a naive version of it using `tz_localize`. 

```
>>> ts = pd.Timestamp(year=2021, month = 3, day = 14, hour = 2, minute = 15, tz = 'America/New_York')
In __new__
America/New_York
<class 'str'>
In maybe_get_tz
5
In maybe_get_tz
>>> ts
Timestamp('2021-03-14 02:15:00-0500', tz='America/New_York')
>>> naive_ts = pd.Timestamp(year=2021, month = 3, day = 14, hour = 2, minute = 15)
In __new__
None
<class 'NoneType'>
In maybe_get_tz
>>> naive_ts.tz_localize('America/New_York')
In localize
In maybe_get_tz
5
in get_dst_info
In __new__
None
<class 'NoneType'>
In maybe_get_tz
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "pandas/_libs/tslibs/timestamps.pyx", line 1295, in pandas._libs.tslibs.timestamps.Timestamp.tz_localize
    value = tz_localize_to_utc_single(self.value, tz,
  File "pandas/_libs/tslibs/tzconversion.pyx", line 74, in pandas._libs.tslibs.tzconversion.tz_localize_to_utc_single
    return tz_localize_to_utc(
  File "pandas/_libs/tslibs/tzconversion.pyx", line 330, in pandas._libs.tslibs.tzconversion.tz_localize_to_utc
    raise pytz.NonExistentTimeError(stamp)
pytz.exceptions.NonExistentTimeError: 2021-03-14 02:15:00
```
So we could be doing something wrong or not realizing something but it seems like the `Timestamp.__new__` method just doesn't check for nonexistent times. From what we can tell, our timezone in the first example is being handled by the `maybe_get_tz` method's fifth if statement that seems to simply release it to the `pytz` package in the singlehanded line `tz = pytz.timezone(tz)` which may mean that `pandas` has no innate way of checking new timestamp's time zones at this point.

Let me know if you're able to trace the problem more or if you have any insights. Sorry for the wall of text.

Update: We think that we managed to resolve this issue by making a naive timestamp and then checking it against the user-requested timezone using `tz_localize_to_utc_single`. We'll be adding test cases and making a PR soon.
